page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server virtualized via KVM. It features an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. For hardware acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage solutions, and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specialized workloads. The single-threaded gzip compression at 35.51 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.51 GB/sec rank in the top tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 182.09 GB/sec. For LLM inference using a small 135M model, the server achieves top-tier throughput with 10515.12 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 547.27 tokens/sec for text generation. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core at 26217.73 and PassMark CPU at 32078.76, fall within the average tier, reflecting the shared CPU allocation model.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for GPU-centric and memory-heavy workloads due to the inclusion of the H100 accelerator paired with a massive 240.0 GB RAM footprint. However, the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent clear tradeoffs for workloads requiring sustained, dedicated CPU performance or high-speed local disk I/O. This configuration is highly suited for large language model inference, deep learning training, data science pipelines, and memory-intensive GPU-accelerated computing.
description: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a KVM-based, GPU-accelerated server designed for memory-intensive and parallel computing workloads. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor offering 12 vCPUs on a shared allocation model, 240.0 GB of system memory, and a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of VRAM. The server does not include local storage, meaning external storage must be attached. In benchmark testing, the instance delivers top-tier performance in single-threaded compression and small-model LLM inference, processing 10515.12 tokens/sec for prompts. Standard multi-core CPU and memory benchmarks perform in the average tier. This hardware profile is highly efficient for GPU-driven tasks that require substantial memory capacity but can tolerate shared CPU resources, making it a strong fit for machine learning inference, data science, and memory-heavy analytical workloads.
